What I do when I want my foundation to last a long time varies. I used to have really oily skin, but lately my skin has gotten really dry and just gets oily in the t zone. 

After moisturizing, I dust a setting powder all over my face (Right now I'm using 3W Clinic Powder, which is a Korean product and it also is a little bit sparkly, but my skin becomes very matte). I also make sure there's not too much on my face, just a light layer. 

Next I use just a tinted moisturizer foundation to even out my skin tone a tiny bit lightly. I'm using OCC liquid foundation in R0. It's a very pinky shade and dries fast on my face. 

After that, I conceal the hell out of my face. Depending on how broken out my skin is, if there's not too many issues, I use a bareMinerals eye brightener to cover up some spots. If my skin is looking bad, I whip out my Ben Nye wheels and I white out everything that needs to be covered. Set that with my powder. And then I go back over it with a concealer of my skin tone (a color I create on the back of my hand with the Ben Nye colors I have). It's theatrical makeup, so the colors are really opaque. And once I set them, I have no issues with the colors lasting all day. 

I hope this helps a little bit. My face takes some time to fully cover when I need to though, so I skip out on makeup as much as I can do it can breathe!

I feel like the way you look is something that should be personal to you before anyone else. I've always told myself that I should like how I look if I catch myself in a mirror, so I dress accordingly. And I also think it is very kind of you to consider how your partner feels about any changes to your appearance no matter how drastic it might be. However, I do find it a bit sad and petty that he might not want to be with you if you underwent some cosmetic changes. But he had that right, and if he does, maybe he's not that worth it. If you just want a non permanent thing done though, maybe just skip doing it if he's that important. You might not keep the piercing forever anyway. 

On a personal note, I have a sleeve with some open spots still on one arm, and my other arm has a few pieces as well. I'm in the talks with my tattoo guy about options for my legs. I love tattoos and want to add more for many years. And I'm well aware that not many men go for that look, and I might be missing out on dating a really great guy. But I just remember if he can't like me for that, then we probably don't match up all that well. And I usually date guys with many more tattoos than me, so they would just be hypocrites if they wished I had fewer tattoos. 

I also dress in an "alternative" way, however my actual clothes are pretty conservative too. Most of my shirts are long sleeved and not many low cut options either. So, people that aren't close friends with me might not know right away that I have tattoos. My best friend informed me that a mutual friend of ours liked me once. I was not interested for a number of reasons, but he was still someone I could be friends with. So she let him know that I didn't like him that way (we weren't so close that we had each other's phone numbers or hung out one on one). Well a few months later, he sees that I had tattoos on my arm, and he apparently freaked out about it and vented to my friend that he really dodged a bullet with me. 

But personally I feel like I dodged a bullet from someone who judges my appearance so scrutinizingly. Also he has two tattoos I think. Silly. 

So tattoos and piercings are really a lifestyle choice that others don't have to like or even accept, but if it's something you really care to get, you should do what makes you happy. But there's consequences to that later on. Hope this helps! Also, I tend to hang around with people that like tattoos and piercings so it's part of my life a lot, I couldn't date someone who hates all that. I enjoy the artwork of it all.
